How Did the Milky Way Get Its Name?

Well this is interesting. I have read Ovid's Metamorphoses, but the references hardly stuck in my memory. There are much more interesting aspects of that book. The term is certainly of Greek origin in reference to milk, but the academic quoted gave no proper signposts as to its usage beyond that. I'd quibble with the assertion that it originated in "European countries", especially as Alexandria in Egypt was the major intellectual center of Hellenistic times after the early 4th century BC, and a lot of astronomical observations in the ancient world originated there as well as in Asia Minor. But that's a quibble. The 'Milky Way' was undoubtedly described in other ancient texts. Babylonia, Egypt and China come to mind. In the case of the first was the term borrowed from the Near East rather than being a Greek invention. Damned if I know. It bears looking into.
Off the subject, but I often wonder how much more advanced we'd be as a civilization if the Library of Alexandria hadn't been burnt to the ground. Such an irrational waste of knowledge.
